'''Targa Resources Pipeline System''' is a natural gas pipeline in the United States, with 6 segments.

==Location==
Forza Gas Pipeline: The pipeline is proposed to run from Targa Northern Delaware Red Hills Plant, New Mexico to Wildcat Junction Station, Texas.<ref name="r463e77">{{Cite web|url=https://www.targaresources.com/static-files/3f119e57-5bac-4fd9-930f-8305620cd99d|title=Forza Pipeline open season notice|website=targaresources.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="rf931ac">{{Cite web|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260516021700/https://www.targaresources.com/natural-gas-pipelines|title=https://web.archive.org/web/20260516021700/https://www.targaresources.com/natural-gas-pipelines|website=web.archive.org|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="r30800f">{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx|title=Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, U.S. Energy Information Administration, August 2026|website=eia.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>
Buffalo Run Gas Pipeline: The pipeline is located in Texas.<ref name="r48735a">{{Cite web|url=https://www.targaresources.com/static-files/8c3ab5dc-9abb-4152-8e45-61e8eddb4674|title=Targa Resources Corp. Investor Presentation, November 2025|website=targaresources.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="r30800f" />
Bull Run Gas Pipeline: The pipeline is located in Texas.<ref name="r48735a" />
Buffalo Run Extension: The pipeline is located in Texas.<ref name="r48735a" /><ref name="r30800f" />
Bull Run Extension: The pipeline is proposed to run from Wildcat Junction Station, Texas to Waha, Texas.<ref name="r30800f" />

==Background==
===Forza Gas Pipeline===
Forza is a proposed Targa natural gas pipeline in the Delaware Basin. Targa Resources said Forza Pipeline LLC would build about 36 miles of 36-inch pipe from Lea County, New Mexico to near the Wildcat Junction Station in Winkler County, Texas.<ref name="r463e77" /> Forza would also lease 43 miles of capacity on the Bull Run Extension to reach the Waha hub.<ref name="r463e77" /> The open season notice said it would provide about 750,000 Dth/d of firm capacity.<ref name="r463e77" /> Targa announced the project in November 2025 and filed a certificate application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on December 3, 2025.<ref name="rc86f12">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1389170/000119312526337729/trgp-20260630.htm|title=Targa Resources Corp. quarterly report (Form 10-Q) for the quarter ended June 30, 2026|website=sec.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref> In its quarterly report for the period ending June 2026, Targa said operations were expected to begin in the middle of 2028, pending regulatory approvals.<ref name="rc86f12" />

===Buffalo Run Gas Pipeline===
Buffalo Run is a Targa natural gas pipeline project in Texas. Targa announced it on September 30, 2025.<ref name="recfa33" /> It has two parts. One is a new 35-mile pipeline linking several Targa plants in the Permian Midland. The other is the conversion of an existing 55-mile Targa pipeline to natural gas service, which would link Targa's Midland and Delaware systems.<ref name="recfa33" /> Targa said the project would be completed in stages and be fully complete in early 2028.<ref name="recfa33" /> The Energy Information Administration listed it as announced, at about 90 miles in total, with a 2028 in-service year.<ref name="r30800f" />

===Bull Run Gas Pipeline===
Bull Run is an existing Targa intrastate natural gas pipeline in the Delaware Basin in Texas.<ref name="rc86f12" /> The Energy Information Administration described it as Targa's existing 42-inch Bull Run Pipeline.<ref name="r30800f" /> Targa announced a 43-mile extension of it in August 2025.<ref name="rc86f12" />

===Buffalo Run Extension===
Targa's announcements do not describe a Buffalo Run Extension separate from the Buffalo Run project. A November 2025 Targa investor presentation listed Buffalo Run at about 90 miles, to be completed by early 2028.<ref name="r48735a" />

===Bull Run Extension===
The Bull Run Extension is a Targa intrastate natural gas pipeline in the Delaware Basin. It would add about 43 miles of 42-inch pipe to the existing Bull Run pipeline, from Wildcat Junction Station in Winkler County, Texas to the Waha hub.<ref name="r30800f" /> Targa announced the extension in August 2025.<ref name="rc86f12" /> A November 2025 investor presentation gave an in-service date of the first quarter of 2027.<ref name="r48735a" /> The Energy Information Administration said the extension would also carry the capacity leased to the Forza pipeline, and listed service as targeted for the second quarter of 2028.<ref name="r30800f" />

===Bull Run II Pipeline===
Targa announced Bull Run II on August 18, 2026, together with new 20-year agreements with ExxonMobil. The line would be added to Targa's existing Bull Run residue gas system. It would carry gas from three planned Delaware basin processing plants, Wrangler, Ranger and Ranger II.<ref name="r2ebb68" /><ref name="rca4bf9" />

The plants would total about 825 million cubic feet per day. Take-or-pay commitments would back the pipeline. Targa said it expected operations to begin in the first half of 2028.<ref name="r2ebb68" /><ref name="rca4bf9" />
